$comment: The product site's own facts, as data: which pack is the ground, which mode a
visitor gets who has never chosen, and the set of products the switcher moves
between. A pack identifier is a token, and this file is the one place a site
picks one, so a renamed or retired pack is a compile error rather than a page
that quietly inherits the ground. The records treat the page ground and a
product's mark as two different axes: the ground is stable for the life of the
page, and a product's mark comes from this directory.
The five products are the five repositories that coordinate. Four of them are
not this site, which is why the header carries a switcher at all: a set that has
to tell five things apart is the reason five packs are on one page. This site's
own mark wears the page's own pack, so its boundary is the ground rather than a
`tagline` is here rather than in the landing because the directory is the one
place a product's own words live, and three of them are read on the landing as
product rows. It was there before this migration too, in the shared registry the
old chrome read; the words did not change, only the file they are read from, and
the two that carried an em-dash now carry a colon, because a dash used as
punctuation is the most recognisable tell of a page nobody wrote.
